# Key sequences (keybind = ctrl+b>v=new_split:right): a prefix key is held
# back until the next key says what it was. The config binds ctrl+b>v,
# ctrl+b>ctrl+b (the prefix itself, for the program) and cmd+k>cmd+u.
type:cat -v
key:enter
wait:0.5
# A key that isn't part of a sequence: cat gets the prefix after all, then the key.
# (Its tag reads on its ground in the appearance the pane has, changed while it shows too.)
appearance:dark
key:ctrl+b
wait:0.2
expect-not:^B
expect-pending-keys:⌃B …
appearance:light
expect-pending-keys:⌃B …
key:x
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect:^Bx
expect-pending-keys:-
# The prefix twice sends it once.
key:ctrl+b
key:ctrl+b
key:y
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect:^By
expect-not:^B^B
# The prefix, then its key: a split, and cat saw neither.
key:ctrl+b
wait:0.2
expect-panes:1
key:v
wait:0.8
expect-panes:2
expect-focus:2
expect-not:^Bv
# ⌘ keys arrive as key equivalents: the same sequence. (⌘K alone clears
# the screen by default; as a prefix it waits, and the pane keeps its text.)
type:echo MARK-TWO
key:enter
wait:0.5
key:cmd+k
wait:0.3
expect-panes:2
expect:MARK-TWO
expect-pending-keys:⌘K …
key:cmd+u
wait:0.8
expect-panes:3
expect-pending-keys:-
